## Introduction

The supabase connector allows to manage data stored into the *Supabase* PostgreSQL cloud.\
The high-level functions are:

- load_data()
- save_data()

The following parameters are **mandatory**:

- **`api = "supabase"`** : to indicate which connector to use.
- **`url`**: the project url provided by Supabase.\
  Environment variable `"SUPABASE_API_URL"` can be used.
- **`api_key`\***: the API key provided by Supabase.\
  Environment variable `"SUPABASE_API_KEY"` should be used.
- **`table`**: the name of the target table in the database.\
  Environment variable `"SUPABASE_TABLE"` can be used.

::: callout-important
Environment variables are provided to pass the url, api_key and table values.\
While url & table variables are considered as optional to have a single definition, api_key should always be passed through the environment variable so that it is not hard coded anywhere.
:::

## Select data

Specific parameter dedicated to selecting (loading) data:

- query: if not provided, all data in the target table will be loaded.

``` r
# set environment
Sys.setenv("SUPABASE_API_URL" = "https://<project_ref>.supabase.co/rest/v1/")
Sys.setenv("SUPABASE_API_KEY" = "<api_key>")

# select all rows from table 'test'
load_data(api = "supabase", table = "test")
```

See supabase_select() for more details.

## Upsert data

Specific parameter dedicated to creating / updating the data:

- **data**: the data, as a data.frame object.\
  Because upsert is implemented, the data.frame can mix new & updated rows in a single call.

``` r
# set environment
Sys.setenv("SUPABASE_API_URL" = "https://<project_ref>.supabase.co/rest/v1/")
Sys.setenv("SUPABASE_API_KEY" = "<api_key>")

# insert rows (assuming the test table has id & comment attributes)
save_data(api = "supabase", table = "test", data = data.frame(id = 2, comment = "test"))

# update rows
save_data(api = "supabase", table = "test", data = data.frame(id = 2, comment = "update"))

# upsert rows
save_data(api = "supabase", table = "test", data = data.frame(id = 2, comment = "update again"),
                                            id = 3, comment = "new rows")
```

See supabase_upsert() for more details.

## Delete data

Specific parameters dedicated to deleting data:

- key: the name of the primary key attribute, in case it is not "id".
- **values**: the index value(s) to be deleted.

``` r
# set environment
Sys.setenv("SUPABASE_API_URL" = "https://<project_ref>.supabase.co/rest/v1/")
Sys.setenv("SUPABASE_API_KEY" = "<api_key>")

# delete rows
save_data(api = "supabase", table = "test", values = c(1, 2))
```

## List

The high-level functions are smart enough to understand parameters passed as a list.

For example:

``` r
load_data(api = "supabase", table = "test")
```

Is equivalent to:

``` r
save_data(connector = list(api = "supabase", table = "test"))
```

This is useful when several connectors may be used in the same app or when the connector values are stored as a list-like object (a YAML file for example).
